![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062908/assets/ab11a3dde0aebbd4088c498e37da48909f9a309ca9d4ab29bfcfa788d53e5c5e.png)

One branch of a hyperbola (shown above) is defined by the parametric equations

$$
x=4\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t.
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $t?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of the full hyperbola are

$$
x=4\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,\pi ],\,t\ne \pm \frac{\pi }{2}.
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a single branch, we refer to the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14062908/assets/f825ca9f9431ca38b14ed141639d5cf4189f0fde0526e943ddb956e112c3e4ab.png)

We can see that if we restrict $t$ to $[-\pi ,-\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $(\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ],$ we get only the lower branch.

Therefore, the parametric equations that describe only the lower branch are

$$
x=4\operatorname{tan}⁡t,\,y=3\operatorname{sec}⁡t,\,t\in [-\pi ,-\frac{\pi }{2})\cup (\frac{\pi }{2},\pi ].
$$
